title: Scroll paper peel (corner folds flat as you scroll)
description: The trevornoah.com hero peel: a square 'page' folds its top-right corner over along a diagonal crease as you scroll. It is a FLAT fold, not a 3D rotation — the flap is the page content clipped to the corner triangle and reflected across the crease (matrix(0,1,1,0,0,0) mirror about the top-left origin, then translated so the crease endpoints stay pinned), so it reads as the mirrored underside of the paper. A second layer shows through the cut. Scrubbed to scroll position, so scrolling down folds and scrolling back up un-folds — the fold tracks scroll direction.

params.front_clip: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - L) 0, 100% L, 100% 100%, 0 100%)  — removes the top-right triangle
params.flap_clip: polygon(calc(100% - L) 0, 100% 0, 100% L)  — the removed triangle, clipped in local space
params.flap_transform: translate(calc(100% - L), calc(L - 100%)) matrix(0,1,1,0,0,0)  — reflect across the diagonal crease, endpoints pinned
params.L: calc(--p * 100%)  (page is square so % maps to a true 45deg crease)
params.progress: --p 0..1 scrubbed from how far the sticky stage has scrolled through its own height, eased in-out
params.note: The site's peeled layer is a flat matrix3d mirror with preserve-3d; the fold mechanism (clip + reflected back + diagonal crease) is verified from the live DOM. The exact scroll-to-progress curve is a clean reconstruction — the site drives it via Webflow IX2 which didn't expose per-scroll keyframes to scripting.

a11y: prefers-reduced-motion: no scrubbing — the page is shown flat and fully readable, the flap is hidden and the section collapses to normal flow.
